intent: The chevron that marks a trigger as expandable and turns over while its item is open.
typical_uses: Rendered by NavigationMenuTrigger after its caption; never placed by the caller in the ordinary composition

instead.note: NavigationMenuTrigger already renders one NavigationMenuIcon after its caption.

dont_use_when.situation: The arrow that points from the open trigger at the popup

invariants.text: The icon reads its open state from the nearest NavigationMenuItem and throws when rendered outside one.
The icon carries `data-popup-open`, and turns over, only while the menu is open on its own item; it is hidden from assistive technology.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the kit's chevron; a caller's `render` replaces the chevron element together with the classes the kit and `className` put on it

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies, including the kit's own chevron
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the icon's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. The kit itself passes the chevron through `render` and spreads the caller's props after it.

style.states: style accepts a function of the icon's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The icon as the trigger renders it

bad.title: An icon with no item around it
bad.why: The icon reads its open state from the nearest NavigationMenuItem; outside one the primitive throws.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, NavigationMenuIconState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies, including the kit's own chevron. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the icon's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. The kit itself passes the chevron through `render` and spreads the caller's props after it.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: NavigationMenuIconState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the icon's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.
